key_points: You weigh about seventy kilograms. A blue whale can reach a hundred and fifty thousand. The Eiffel Tower, about ten million.
Every human alive, put together: around four hundred billion. The whole Earth: six trillion trillion.
The Sun outweighs three hundred and thirty thousand Earths. And a neutron star squeezes even more into a ball the size of a city.
The black hole at the centre of our galaxy weighs four million Suns, packed smaller than Mercury's orbit.
All the ordinary matter we can see comes to about fifty-three zeros of kilograms. And dark matter outweighs it five to one.
concept_options.title: How Heavy Can Anything Get?
concept_options.visual_approach: 'Weight Column': the ladder engine pointing UP again, in kilograms (log10 kg, 1 kg at the bottom to 10^37 kg near the top), a heavy bronze-white marker that CLIMBS rung by rung (YOU, BLUE WHALE, EIFFEL TOWER, ALL HUMANS, EARTH, SUN / NEUTRON STAR, SGR A*), a ZEROS counter 1 -> 36, a drawn rail BREAK and a dashed line for the observable universe's ordinary matter at 10^53 where the counter jumps to 53; then a DARK MATTER bar five times taller rises behind it (drawn, PROBABLY). Window with three AI plates (blue whale, Eiffel Tower, neutron star) and a drawn black hole with Mercury's orbit for scale.
concept_options.core_message: Each step up adds zeros; after 53 of them, most of the mass is still something we can't see.
concept_options.cta: What's the heaviest thing you've ever lifted?
concept_options.tone: curious, building, then a quiet deadpan close
concept_options.why_this_works: Completes the 'How X can it get' set (loud, cold, hot) with the same log-ladder grammar viewers already know, reusing video 13's ladder and counter code. The 'you're doing 100,000 km/h right now' beat puts the viewer on the scale. Risk: same engine as video 13 - re-dressed (no black-body colour, white-cyan marker, speed streaks) and the twist is different (a wall, not a fray).

key_points: A grain of sand is about half a millimetre. A human hair is a tenth of that. And that's about where your eyes give up.
A red blood cell is ten times smaller again. Most viruses are smaller still, too small for any ordinary microscope to see.
An atom is a thousand times smaller than a virus. And the proton at its centre is sixty thousand times smaller than the atom.
Electrons are so small that no experiment has found any size at all. Below that, physicists point to the Planck length, twenty more zeros down.
Thirty-four zeros after the decimal point. Maybe that's the floor. Or maybe there isn't one.

selected_concept.rationale: Third in the extremes series (16 speed, 17 size); reuses the ladder engine (lean), new payoff: dark matter outweighing everything on the ladder.

taste_profile.design_read: Youth science short: a calm climb up one speed ladder, from walking to light, ending at a wall that never moves.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Night ink sky, steel rail, ONE white-cyan accent for the marker; no temperature colours; red only for 'c' (the wall).
taste_profile.layout_variation: Log rail + marker, zeros counter, window plates, the LHC nines readout.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Numbers from the brief only; AI stills as short tagged inserts.
anti_patterns: 'the falcon is the fastest animal' as fact without the dive caveat
quality_gates: Every rung's number matches the brief

tools.role: fact verification (3 searches, 9 sources, 11 data points)

stages.approach: Complete. Falcon dive ~390 km/h kept as PROBABLY (weak sourcing); cheetah 'about a hundred' (collar 95, track 103); snail dropped.
This document; approval gate. No paid generation has run.
~106 spoken words in 5 sections; closing line complete.
~12 scenes; hero beats: 'sitting still you're doing 100,000' and the marker stopping short of 'c' while the nines fill. Last scene: calm, finished.

tools.role: narration, Bella hpp4J3VqNfWAUOO0d1Us, eleven_v4, 1 take per section (retake only on failed Whisper QA, max 2)

3 stills x 1: S1 cheetah at full sprint (AI impression); S2 peregrine falcon in a steep dive, wings tucked (AI impression); S3 a heat-shielded spacecraft close to the Sun (AI impression of the Parker Solar Probe)
1 bed that slowly gains energy (light synth pulse + strings, ~100 BPM, steady loudness), resolved final chord with ring-out
6 x 1: soft whoosh (rung climb), sonic thump (sound barrier, soft), digit tick (counter), low hum (probe), high shimmer (light), soft glass 'tink' (the wall)

stages.approach: estimate_only before every run; narration first; stills QA (9:16 2K, no faces, no text); clips only from passing stills; globe, maps (real coastline data), readouts, tiles, captions and tab are code at $0.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: Failed still -> code glow/thermal panel (no re-roll). Failed clip -> slow code parallax on the still.

stages.approach: Music ducked ~12 dB; SFX on visible landings (lessons 4, 22) and phone-band checked (lesson 5); last word 'know' >= +12 dB over bed in 300-4000 Hz AND broadband within ~3 dB of its sentence (lessons 18, 30); final chord ~0.15 s after 'know', ~1.5 s settle.
Atelier render; check_hooks + full 0.25-scale test; finish_master.sh (-14 LUFS, <= -1 dBTP); upload copy at maxrate ~12M only if the master passes ~60 MB (lesson 21); three independent QA agents.
